newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah kill Israeli soldier in Lebanon clash.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah kill Israeli soldier in Lebanon clash.

text.p: One Israeli soldier was killed and another wounded on Sunday in a clash with Hizbollah guerrillas in deepening violence in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas claimed responsibility for the attack.

The death brought the toll in the bloodiest week in south Lebanon since an Israeli offensive in April 1996 to 15: one Israeli soldier, a pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman, six members of Hizbollah and seven Lebanese civilians.
Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri discussed "Israel's escalation of aggression" with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus, a presidential spokesman said.
"Israel, by increasing escalation through raids and shelling of Lebanese lands, is seeking to push the situation in the region to a chasm and a state of explosion," Damascus radio said.

"This policy of (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu ... is to destroy the peace process, pull it up by the roots, sabotage its results and take the region back to the darkest days of tension."
Hizbollah said its fighters ambushed an Israeli motorised patrol with machinegun fire and rocket-propelled grenades in the area of Mleikh south of Jizzine, inside Israel's occupation zone.
The attack brought to 13 the number of Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon since the beginning of the year.
In retaliation, Israeli artillerymen shelled Lebanese-held areas facing Kfar Houneh. There was no immediate report on casualties in the bombardment.

Earlier, Lebanese security sources said a five-year-old Lebanese girl was hurt when a shell hit an orphanage in the area of Jizzine, officially outside the occupation zone but under the control of the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia.
An Israeli army spokesman said the injured were a woman and a 15-year-old girl. They said the orphanage had been hit by Katyusha rockets fired by "terrorists".
A mine exploded earlier in the day near a truck in the village of Marqaba inside the occupation zone. No one was injured, according to SLA militia sources.
The attacks come amid the worst border violence between Lebanese and Israeli forces since the Jewish state's 17-day blitz on the country in April 1996 that killed 200 Lebanese, mostly civilians.
Under the ceasefire that ended that fighting, both sides agreed not to target civilians or fire from civilian areas. Israel and Lebanon traded charges last week of violation of the agreement.
Lebanon pointed to the large number of civilian casualties it suffered while Israel protested against a rocket attack on Friday that wounded a woman inside Israel.

Hizbollah guerrillas, fighting to drive Israeli troops from the south Lebanon occupation zone, said they did not fire the rockets. Israeli aircraft later attacked sites of both Hizbollah and a radical Palestinian faction.
